definitions.explanation: A freshwater fish of the carp family, native to Japan and widely found in rivers, lakes, and ponds. Culturally significant in Japanese cuisine, literature, and proverbs.

examples.japanese: {池|いけ}で{鮒|ふな}を{釣|つ}った。
examples.english: I caught a crucian carp in the pond.

examples.japanese: {琵琶湖|びわこ}の{鮒寿司|ふなずし}は{有名|ゆうめい}な{郷土|きょうど}{料理|りょうり}だ。
examples.english: Funazushi from Lake Biwa is a famous local dish.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どものころ、{近所|きんじょ}の{川|かわ}でよく{鮒|ふな}を{捕|つか}まえて{遊|あそ}んだものだ。
examples.english: When I was a child, I used to catch crucian carp in the nearby river and play with them.

notes:
A common freshwater fish in Japan, smaller and rounder than koi. It has been part of Japanese food culture for centuries, particularly in the form of {鮒寿司|ふなずし}, a fermented sushi from Shiga Prefecture considered a precursor to modern sushi.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鮒寿司|ふなずし}: fermented crucian carp sushi (Shiga specialty)
- {鮒釣|ふなつ}り: crucian carp fishing
- {金魚|きんぎょ}の{祖先|そせん}は{鮒|ふな}: goldfish descend from crucian carp

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {鮒|ふな}の{仲間|なかま}には{鮒|ふな}: like attracts like (lit. among crucian carp, only crucian carp)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {鯉|こい}: koi, common carp — larger and more elongated
- {金魚|きんぎょ}: goldfish — domesticated variety originally bred from crucian carp
